newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX ELECTRICITY FALLS WITH CASH, COOLER WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX ELECTRICITY FALLS WITH CASH, COOLER WEATHER.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended lower Tuesday on declining physical power prices and expectations for cooler temperatures in some key metropolitan centers, industry sources said.

Palo Verde (PV) finished down $1.30 at $30.51 per megawatt hour (MWh) after trades at $30.50-31.30 per MWh, while October closed down 81 cents at $23.49 after exchanges in a range of $23.45-23.80 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds settled between 66 cents lower and 35 cents higher.
September California Oregon Border (COB) ended down 50 cents at $23.10 following exchanges at $22.90-23.30, while October closed down 21 cents at $22.80 per MWh after trades at $22.55-22.80 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 396 COB and 808 PV contracts traded Tuesday.
"The dailies have fallen off quite a bit," said one Western power trader, adding balance-of-the month prices at PV have fallen about $5.00 per MWh since last Tuesday.
Next-day peak power markets at COB and PV were also said to have eased slightly on Tuesday for Wednesday delivery.
"We're also seeing a bit of a cooling trend in Los Angeles," the trader also said.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to average four to six degrees Fahrenheit below normal across the east, one to three degrees below normal through the central regions, and near to three degrees above normal across the west through the week, Weather Services Corp said.
In the Southwest, temperatures were seen near to three degrees below normal through the northeast and up to three degrees above normal across the south and west this week.
Los Angeles was expected to see a maximum temperature near 74 degrees Wednesday and near 76 degrees Thursday.

In generation news, restart of the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 3 at the Navajo coal-fired power plant near Page, Ariz., was delayed to Tuesday afternoon due to a boiler tube leak, a spokesman for the plant said Tuesday.
The unit, which was shut over the weekend for repairs, had been expected to restart late Monday. Navajo's other two 750 MW units were said to be operating normally.

The 700 MW unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was scheduled to restart Tuesday afternoon after being shut late Friday for unplanned repairs, sources familiar with the plant's operations said. The plant's other 700 MW unit, as well as two smaller 330 MW units, were said to be operating normally.

Separately, southbound transmission capacity on the Pacific Intertie will be cut by 350 MW to 850 MW during certain hours on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of this week, according to the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA).
